data_center.analysis: Available records list 3,068 operating sites and 1,556 sites in development, equivalent to roughly one development site for every two operating sites. Separately, 894 sites are tracked in the active pipeline. Recent reports identify two concrete execution risks: a Texas moratorium on data-center approvals was broadened to include environmental permits, while Oracle issued a force majeure notice following setbacks at Project Jupiter. These cases do not establish a failure rate for the wider pipeline, but they show why site counts should not be read as completed capacity.

macro.analysis: Market support has strengthened, but not evenly. The AI Equity Index rose materially to 35.9, while the share of companies with positive one-year returns edged up to 63.7% and the median return slipped to 13.1%. CNBC reported that Micron beat earnings estimates and issued strong guidance as data-center revenue increased elevenfold. That result shows substantial demand in one part of the hardware chain, but the market measures still point to uneven gains across the wider group. The investment cycle retains internal financial support: operating cash flow covers current CapEx 1.42 times. Yet cash reserves equal 0.96 years of CapEx, borrower strain stands at 26.0 and lender strain is -13.5. The physical side has a similar split. Electric-power construction grew 10.8%, but only 24.2% of the 2,061 GW active interconnection queue has reached an executed-agreement or construction stage. Spending and construction are active; the harder question is how much proposed capacity can clear financing and grid connection. Execution is also increasingly local. Available records contain 1,556 sites in development, about half the 3,068 operating sites. Construction Dive reports that public support is emerging as a data-center bottleneck, while the drought screen now places 24.4% of campuses with county data in counties containing some D2-or-worse drought; 22.2% are in counties where at least a quarter of the area is affected. County overlap does not establish site-level drought or water demand, and these developments do not show how many projects will be delayed. They reinforce why development-site counts should not be treated as completed capacity.

power.analysis: Commercial electricity demand growth increased slightly to 3.1%, while total retail demand growth eased to 1.2%. Net planned generation additions through the pipeline horizon slipped to 225.2 GW, and retail electricity price growth eased slightly to 4.4%. Google reportedly agreed to support nuclear uprates at Georgia Power's Vogtle and Hatch plants, providing one route to additional output from existing facilities. It does not establish when the wider planned pipeline will be delivered.

The stricter screen—at least 25% of the county under D2-or-worse drought—covers 318 campuses, or 22.2%. Both measures increased materially.
